questions.question:
**Identify the part of the sentence that contains a grammatical error.**

A. It is imperative that he B. understands the severity of the situation C. and that he makes D. a clear, concise, and decisive statement to the press.

options.text: understands the severity of the situation
a clear, concise, and decisive statement to the press.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence requires the **subjunctive mood** because it begins with the phrase "**It is imperative that...**"
 
• After certain "demand" or "necessity" adjectives (such as *imperative, essential, crucial, important*) followed by "that," the verb must be in its **base form** (the infinitive without "to"), regardless of the subject.
 
• Therefore, "**understands**" should be "**understand**." (Note: Part C also contains the same error with "makes," which should be "make," but Part B is the first instance of this grammatical violation).
 
• Thus, the primary error is located in **part B** (Option 2) of the sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"It is imperative that he **understand** the severity of the situation and that he **make** a clear, concise, and decisive statement to the press."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **A: "It is imperative that he"** – This part correctly introduces the subjunctive clause.
 
• **C: "and that he makes"** – While this also contains a subjunctive error (it should be "make"), in multiple-choice questions, the first error or the one provided in the key option is targeted.
 
• **D: "a clear, concise, and decisive statement to the press."** – This part is grammatically correct and uses the Oxford comma and adjectives properly.
 
• **The Subjunctive Mood:** We use the base form of the verb (*be, go, work, understand*) for all persons. Example: "I suggest that he **be** on time" instead of "he is."

questions.question:
**Identify the part of the sentence that contains a grammatical error.**

A. The new employee B. seems to be C. a fast learner D. and more smarter than the last one.

options.text: and more smarter than the last one

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The primary issue in the sentence is the use of a **double comparative** ("**more smarter**").
 
• In English, comparative adjectives are formed either by adding the suffix "**-er**" (for short words like *smart*) or by using the word "**more**" (for longer words like *intelligent*).
 
• You should never use both at the same time. Since "smarter" is already in the comparative form, "more" is redundant and grammatically incorrect.
 
• Thus, the error is located in **part D** (Option 4) of the sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"The new employee seems to be a fast learner **and smarter than** the last one."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **A: "The new employee"** – This is the subject of the sentence and is grammatically correct.
 
• **B: "seems to be"** – This linking verb phrase correctly connects the subject to the predicate.
 
• **C: "a fast learner"** – This is a correctly structured noun phrase acting as a complement.
 
• **Comparative Rules:** Use "-er" for one-syllable adjectives (*faster, taller*). Use "more" for adjectives with three or more syllables (*more beautiful, more expensive*). For two-syllable adjectives, the rule varies, but "smarter" is the standard for "smart."

questions.solution:

__ 
 
• The phrasal verb "**live up to**" means to meet or fulfill expectations, standards, or promises. 
 
• The sentence discusses the failure of a startup to fulfill expectations, so "**live up to**" is the most appropriate choice. 
 
• **Options 1, 2**, and 4 do not convey the intended meaning in this context. 
 
Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**. 
 
**Complete Sentence:** *"The startup failed to **live up to**__ the expectations it had generated among investors."* 
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__** 
 
 
• **Option 1: "live down"** means to overcome or make others forget a shameful or embarrassing event, which is irrelevant here. 
 
• **Option 2: "live through"** means to survive or endure a difficult experience, which does not fit the context. 
 
• **Option 4: "live over"** is not a standard phrasal verb in English and is therefore incorrect.

questions.question: Which of the following is the most compelling ethical argument against autonomous weapons in combat?

options.text: The potential for increased civilian casualties
The speed at which autonomous weapons operate
The transfer of life-and-death decision-making to machines
The lack of accountability in AI decisions

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**Option 3**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ***Analyzing the ethical arguments in the passage:***

 
 
• The second paragraph explicitly and directly answers this question. It states: "The most compelling argument is the transfer of the life-and-death decision-making from a human to a machine."
 
• The text explains that opponents believe this is the core issue because a computer or machine lacks the "moral calculus, compassion, or comprehension of human dignity" required to make ethical judgments about taking a human life.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **The transfer of life-and-death decision-making to machines.**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1 (The potential for increased civilian casualties)**: Incorrect because the passage actually presents the opposite point as a *supporting* argument for the weapons: supporters contend AWS might "decrease civilian casualties" due to accuracy.
 
• **Option 2 (The speed at which autonomous weapons operate)**: Incorrect because the speed (operating with "rapidity") is listed in the first paragraph as a strategic advantage and a reason supporters favor the technology, not an argument against it.
 
• **Option 4 (The lack of accountability in AI decisions)**: Incorrect. While accountability and the "black box" of AI are major concerns discussed in the passage, the author specifically reserves the phrase "most compelling argument" for the transfer of the decision-making process itself.

questions.question: According to the passage, what is the primary concern regarding the integration of AI into modern warfare?

options.text: The technology will never be able to operate in war zones
Autonomous weapons may lack the moral responsibility to make life-and-death decisions
It would be illegal under international laws of armed conflict
AI could be hacked and used against states

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**Option 2**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ***Analyzing the primary concern in the passage:***

 
 
• The passage emphasizes that the core ethical dilemma is the "transfer of the life-and-death decision-making from a human to a machine."
 
• It explicitly states that opponents believe a computer "could never have the moral calculus, compassion, or comprehension of human dignity to make such judgments."
 
• Therefore, the primary concern driving the ethical debate is that autonomous weapons inherently lack the moral responsibility and human judgment required to make life-and-death decisions in combat.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Autonomous weapons may lack the moral responsibility to make life-and-death decisions.**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1 (The technology will never be able to operate in war zones)**: Incorrect because the passage suggests the opposite. Supporters argue AWS might "operate with more accuracy and rapidity in an unpredictable environment."
 
• **Option 3 (It would be illegal under international laws of armed conflict)**: Incorrect because while the passage notes that AWS "tests the very foundations of the international laws of armed conflict," it frames their use as a fiercely debated issue awaiting clear norms, not as an established illegality.
 
• **Option 4 (AI could be hacked and used against states)**: Incorrect because the passage focuses entirely on the ethical dilemmas of the AI's autonomous decision-making (the "black box") and accountability, rather than the threat of hacking or cyber hijacking.

questions.question: In the passage, the term "moral calculus" refers to:

options.text: The ability to make ethical decisions
The efficiency of AI systems in combat

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**Option 2**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ***Analyzing the term "moral calculus":***

 
 
• In the passage, the term "moral calculus" is grouped together with "compassion" and "comprehension of human dignity."
 
• It is used to describe the uniquely human capacity that opponents argue computers lack when tasked with making life-and-death judgments.
 
• While "calculus" usually implies math, in philosophical and ethical contexts, a "moral calculus" refers to the process of weighing right and wrong, evaluating ethical variables, and arriving at a humane, ethical decision.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **The ability to make ethical decisions.**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1 (A complex mathematical process)**: Incorrect because the word "calculus" is being used metaphorically in an ethical sense, not literally to describe mathematics.
 
• **Option 3 (The calculation of military strategies)**: Incorrect because the passage separates strategic advantage (which AI might have) from the ethical, human judgment required to take a life (which AI lacks).
 
• **Option 4 (The efficiency of AI systems in combat)**: Incorrect because efficiency is precisely what supporters claim AI possesses, whereas "moral calculus" is specifically identified as something AI is missing.

questions.question: What is the primary ethical concern raised by the "black box" nature of AI decision-making in AWS?

options.text: It increases the speed of decision-making
It makes it difficult to assign moral and legal culpability
It reduces the potential for civilian casualties

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**Option 3**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ***Analyzing the "black box" concern:***

 
 
• The passage states that the secrecy of AI's decision-making process is commonly known as a "black box."
 
• It explicitly links this "black box" nature to the "difficulty in assigning blame." Because we cannot transparently see how the machine arrived at its decision to kill, it becomes almost impossible to determine who is responsible (the programmer, the commander, or the state) if the weapon kills without authorization.
 
• Therefore, the primary ethical concern is that this opacity makes it profoundly difficult to establish moral and legal culpability.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **It makes it difficult to assign moral and legal culpability.**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1 (It increases the speed of decision-making)**: Incorrect because increased speed is cited as a potential strategic advantage by supporters, not an ethical concern caused by the opacity of the "black box."
 
• **Option 2 (It hinders military efficiency)**: Incorrect because the text suggests autonomous weapons might actually operate with more rapidity and accuracy, thereby potentially increasing efficiency, not hindering it.
 
• **Option 4 (It reduces the potential for civilian casualties)**: Incorrect because this is an argument used by supporters of the technology, whereas the "black box" is presented as a major ethical dilemma regarding accountability.

questions.question: Which argument in favor of autonomous weapons is most strongly supported by proponents?

options.text: They can create more humane warfare
They ensure that no human is ever at risk in combat
They act with more accuracy and rapidity

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**Option 4**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ***Analyzing the proponents' arguments:***

 
 
• The passage explicitly outlines the arguments made by supporters of autonomous weapons in the first paragraph.
 
• It states: "They also might be able to operate with more **accuracy and rapidity** in an unpredictable environment, which could decrease civilian casualties."
 
• While reducing casualties is the ultimate goal, the foundational argument proponents use to support the deployment of these weapons is their inherent technical ability to act faster (rapidity) and with greater precision (accuracy) than human soldiers who suffer from fatigue, fear, and emotional stress.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **They act with more accuracy and rapidity.**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1 (They help reduce civilian casualties)**: Incorrect because while it is a stated benefit, the passage frames it as a secondary outcome ("which could decrease...") resulting directly from the weapons' primary attribute of operating with accuracy and rapidity.
 
• **Option 2 (They can create more humane warfare)**: Incorrect because the passage does not use this terminology. Opponents actually argue that machines lack the compassion or moral calculus to be humane.
 
• **Option 3 (They ensure that no human is ever at risk in combat)**: Incorrect because this is an absolute statement ("no human is ever at risk") that is far too extreme and is not supported by the text.

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences: • **Meticulous** (सावधानीपूर्वक): Showing great attention to detail; very precise and careful. • **Example:** She meticulously planned every detail of the event to ensure its success. • **Fussy** (चुनचुना या झगड़ालू): Hard to please and overly concerned with minor details. • **Example:** The fussy child refused to eat anything but plain pasta. • **Perceptive** (सजग या अनुभवी): Having a keen understanding or insight into something. • **Example:** Her perceptive comments during the discussion impressed everyone in the room. 44:Ta1c, The correct answer is: **Magician**.

questions.question:
**Change the following sentence into the Active form:**

The city council's decision is thought to be influenced by powerful lobbying groups.

options.text: Powerful lobbying groups think that the city council's decision is influenced.
Powerful lobbying groups are thought to influence the city council's decision.
People think that powerful lobbying groups influence the city council's decision.
The city council thinks that powerful lobbying groups influence the decision.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Identify the Complex Passive:** The original sentence "The city council's decision is thought to be influenced..." is a passive construction used for reporting opinions or beliefs.
 
• **Determine the Agent of Belief:** The sentence uses the passive reporting verb "is thought," but doesn't specify who thinks this. In active voice, we use a general subject like **"People," "Many,"** or **"They."**
 
• **Determine the Agent of Influence:** The phrase "to be influenced by powerful lobbying groups" identifies **"powerful lobbying groups"** as the ones performing the action of influencing.
 
• **Structure the Active Sentence:** To make it fully active, we start with the general subject (People) + the active reporting verb (think) + the subordinate clause where the lobbying groups become the subject (powerful lobbying groups influence the city council's decision).

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"People think that powerful lobbying groups influence the city council's decision."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** "Powerful lobbying groups think..." – This changes the meaning; it suggests the groups are the ones holding the opinion, rather than being the ones exerting the influence.
 
• **Option 2:** "are thought to influence" – This is still a passive construction (Passive Reporting Verb).
 
• **Option 4:** "The city council thinks..." – This incorrectly identifies the city council as the agent of the "thinking" action.

questions.question:
**Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect voice:**

The guide said, "We will be exploring the ruins all morning."

options.text: The guide said that they would be exploring the ruins all morning.
The guide said that they will be exploring the ruins all morning.
The guide said that we would be exploring the ruins all morning.
The guide said that we will be exploring the ruins all morning.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Direct Speech:** The guide said, "We will be exploring the ruins all morning."
 
• **Key Conversions:**
 
 
• **Pronoun Change:**
 
 
• The first-person plural pronoun **"We"** in direct speech refers to the guide and the group. When reported by someone else, it typically changes to the third-person plural **"they."**
 
 
 
• **Modal Verb Change (Backshifting):**
 
 
• Since the reporting verb **"said"** is in the past tense, the future modal **"will"** shifts to its past form, **"would."**
 
 
 
• **Tense Maintenance:**
 
 
• The continuous aspect **"be exploring"** remains unchanged after the shifted modal verb.
 
 
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"The guide said that they would be exploring the ruins all morning."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2:** Corrects the pronoun but fails to shift the tense from "will" to "would."
 
• **Option 3:** Corrects the tense but fails to change the pronoun "we" to "they," which is standard in indirect reporting unless the reporter is part of the group.
 
• **Option 4:** Fails to change both the pronoun and the tense.

questions.question:
Choose the most suitable option to replace the highlighted part of the sentence:

Except for **__you and me, no one knew__ **Radha.

options.text: Except for you and I, no one knew Radha
Except for you and me, no one knew Radha
Except you and I, no one knew Radha
Except for I and you, no one knew Radha

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**Except for you and me, no one knew Radha**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase "**Except for you and me**" is grammatically correct because "me" is the appropriate pronoun to follow a preposition like "for."
 
• Option 1 ("**Except for you and I**") is incorrect because the pronoun "I" is used incorrectly after the preposition "for."
 
• Option 3 ("**Except you and I**") is incorrect because the preposition "for" is missing, and "I" is used incorrectly.
 
• Option 4 ("**Except for I and you**") is incorrect because "I" is not the correct form to use after the preposition "for."

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**Complete Sentence:** *"Except for you and me, no one knew Radha."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** "Except for you and I" is incorrect because "I" should not follow a preposition like "for."
 
• **Option 3:** "Except you and I" is incorrect because it omits the preposition "for" and incorrectly uses "I" instead of "me."
 
• **Option 4:** "Except for I and you" is incorrect because "I" is not the correct pronoun to use after "for."

questions.question:
**Choose the correct passive voice transformation of the sentence:**

Why did the brilliant detective suddenly solve the complex mystery?

options.text: Why was the complex mystery suddenly solved by the brilliant detective?
Why was the complex mystery suddenly been solved by the brilliant detective?
Why has the complex mystery been suddenly solved by the brilliant detective?
Why did the complex mystery be solved by the brilliant detective?

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Identify the Tense:** The active sentence "Why did... solve" is an interrogative sentence in the **Simple Past Tense**.
 
• **Interrogative Passive Structure (Simple Past):** The formula is **Wh-word + was/were + Object + Past Participle (V3) + by + Subject?**.
 
• **Step 1:** Keep the question word "Why" at the beginning.
 
• **Step 2:** Use the auxiliary verb "was" because the new subject, "the complex mystery," is singular.
 
• **Step 3:** Convert the main verb "solve" to its third form (V3), which is **"solved."**
 
• **Step 4:** Place the adverb "suddenly" before the main verb for proper flow, and add the agent "by the brilliant detective."

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"Why was the complex mystery suddenly solved by the brilliant detective?"*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2:** "was... been solved" – This is grammatically incorrect; "been" is used with "have/has/had," not with "was" in the simple past passive.
 
• **Option 3:** "has... been suddenly solved" – This changes the tense to Present Perfect Passive, which does not match the original Simple Past "did."
 
• **Option 4:** "did... be solved" – This is an incorrect construction for passive voice questions. "Did" is replaced by "was/were" in the passive form.

questions.question:
**Select the option that expresses the given sentence in direct voice:**

The traveler explained that he was going to visit several historic sites on his trip.

options.text: The traveler said, "He was going to visit several historic sites on his trip."
The traveler said, "He is going to visit several historic sites on his trip."
The traveler explained, "I was going to visit several historic sites on my trip."
The traveler said, "I am going to visit several historic sites on my trip."

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Indirect Speech:** The traveler explained that he was going to visit several historic sites on his trip.
 
• **Key Conversions:**
 
 
• **Pronoun Change:**
 
 
• When shifting to direct speech, the third-person pronouns **"he"** and **"his"** must change to the first-person **"I"** and **"my"** to represent the traveler speaking for himself.
 
 
 
• **Tense Change (Forward-shifting):**
 
 
• The past continuous form **"was going to"** in indirect speech is converted back to the present continuous form **"am going to"** in direct speech to reflect the speaker's original perspective.
 
 
 
• **Reporting Clause:**
 
 
• The conjunction "that" is removed, and the reporting verb (explained/said) is followed by a comma and the quoted speech in quotation marks.
 
 
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"The traveler said, 'I am going to visit several historic sites on my trip.'"*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** Retains the third-person pronoun "he" and the past tense "was," which is grammatically incorrect for direct speech in this context.
 
• **Option 2:** Changes the tense to "is" but fails to change the pronoun to "I," making it sound like the traveler is talking about someone else.
 
• **Option 3:** Correctly changes the pronouns to "I" and "my" but incorrectly keeps the past tense "was," which doesn't fit the direct speech format for a current plan.

questions.question:
**Rearrange the following sentences to form a meaningful and grammatically correct paragraph:**

P. He disassembled the old engine with care, marking each component precisely.

Q. He torqued the bolts to the precise specifications, put in new gaskets, and replaced old parts.

R. After reassembling the engine, he put it back in the vehicle and reattached all of the hoses.

S. On the first turn of the key, the engine flickered to life and resumed its flawless operation.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The paragraph outlines a logical, chronological sequence of a mechanical repair process, moving from teardown to reassembly and testing.
 
• **Sentence P is the first sentence** as it identifies the starting point of the project—the careful disassembly of the machinery:
 
 
• "He disassembled the old engine with care, marking each component precisely."
 
 
 
• **Sentence Q follows** as the middle stage of the repair, focusing on the specific internal maintenance and replacement of parts:
 
 
• "He torqued the bolts to the precise specifications, put in new gaskets, and replaced old parts."
 
 
 
• **Sentence R is the third sentence** because it describes the completion of the reassembly and the physical reinstallation of the engine into its frame:
 
 
• "After reassembling the engine, he put it back in the vehicle and reattached all of the hoses."
 
 
 
• **Sentence S is the fourth sentence** as it provides the satisfying conclusion—the moment the work is tested and proven successful:
 
 
• "On the first turn of the key, the engine flickered to life and resumed its flawless operation."
 
 
 
• The correct sequence is **PQRS**.

 

**Coherent paragraph after rearrangement**:

"He disassembled the old engine with care, marking each component precisely. He torqued the bolts to the precise specifications, put in new gaskets, and replaced old parts. After reassembling the engine, he put it back in the vehicle and reattached all of the hoses. On the first turn of the key, the engine flickered to life and resumed its flawless operation."

questions.question:
**Rearrange the following sentences to form a meaningful and grammatically correct paragraph:**

P: As a result, the software significantly improved operational efficiency across departments

Q: The team worked tirelessly, refining the code and testing each feature for compatibility.

R: It was designed to simplify daily tasks and provide real-time data analysis.

S: A groundbreaking new software was developed to streamline workflow and increase productivity.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The paragraph follows the lifecycle of a software project: from its initial inception and purpose to the labor involved and the final impact on the organization.
 
• **Sentence S is the first sentence** because it introduces the primary subject (the groundbreaking new software) and the overall goal of the project:
 
 
• "A groundbreaking new software was developed to streamline workflow and increase productivity."
 
 
 
• **Sentence R follows** as it uses the pronoun "It" to refer back to the software and elaborates on its specific design features:
 
 
• "It was designed to simplify daily tasks and provide real-time data analysis."
 
 
 
• **Sentence Q is the third sentence** as it describes the developmental effort and quality assurance phase required to make the software functional:
 
 
• "The team worked tirelessly, refining the code and testing each feature for compatibility."
 
 
 
• **Sentence P is the fourth sentence** because it uses the transition phrase "As a result" to conclude the narrative with the successful outcome of the implementation:
 
 
• "As a result, the software significantly improved operational efficiency across departments."
 
 
 
• The correct sequence is **SRQP**.

 

**Coherent paragraph after rearrangement**:

"A groundbreaking new software was developed to streamline workflow and increase productivity. It was designed to simplify daily tasks and provide real-time data analysis. The team worked tirelessly, refining the code and testing each feature for compatibility. As a result, the software significantly improved operational efficiency across departments."
